## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Soceyya Sutta* ("Purity", Iti 66; It 3.17, PTS It 55) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka*. The sutta expounds three kinds of purity or cleanliness (*soceyya*): bodily purity, verbal purity, and mental purity. Text-critical analysis of the collection's metrical summaries notes that the uddāna résumé reflects minor grammatical variations against the prose, utilizing simple adjective forms rather than the abstract noun *soceyya* [Moore 1908].
